lesson.text: Quick memory: share 12 equally between 4 friends and each gets 3. Sharing into equal parts is the key to fractions!
A fraction is a part of a whole that is cut into equal parts. This circle is cut into 4 equal parts, and each part is one quarter: 1/4. The bottom number says how many equal parts there are.
The top number counts the parts we take. 3 of the 4 equal parts are shaded: 3/4, three quarters. 3/4 is 3 parts of size 1/4.
The parts must be equal. This circle has 3 parts, but they are not the same size, so they are not thirds.
A fraction of a set: here are 12 blocks in 4 equal groups. One group is 1/4 of 12: 3 blocks. So 1/4 of 12 = 3.
3/4 of 12 is 3 of those groups: 3 × 3 = 9. First find one part (divide), then take as many parts as the top number says (multiply).
Build it! To fill 3/4 of a wall of 8 blocks: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 blocks in each quarter, and 3 quarters is 6 blocks. Next: fractions on a number line.

exercises.prompt: What fraction of the shape is shaded?
exercises.hint: Count all the equal parts, then the shaded ones.
exercises.explain: 1 of the 4 equal parts is shaded: 1/4.

exercises.prompt: What fraction of the shape is shaded?
exercises.hint: How many equal parts? How many are shaded?
exercises.explain: 1 of the 3 equal parts is shaded: 1/3.

exercises.hint: Look for 2 equal parts with 1 of them shaded.
exercises.explain: The square is cut into 2 equal parts and 1 is shaded: 1/2.

exercises.prompt: This shape is cut into equal parts.
exercises.hint: Would each part cover the others exactly?
exercises.explain: No: some parts are bigger than others.

exercises.prompt: This wall has room for 6 blocks. Fill 1/3 of it.
exercises.hint: Split the 6 spaces into 3 equal parts. How many spaces are in one part?
exercises.explain: 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so 1/3 of the wall is 2 blocks.

exercises.prompt: What fraction of the shape is shaded?
exercises.hint: Count the equal parts and the shaded ones.
exercises.explain: 5 of the 6 equal parts are shaded: 5/6.

exercises.hint: Find 1/3 of 12 first, then take 2 of those parts.
The bottom number is the size of the parts; the top number counts them.
exercises.explain: 3/8 is 3 parts, and each part is 1/8 of the whole.

exercises.prompt: This wall has room for 8 blocks. Fill 3/4 of it.
exercises.hint: 1/4 of 8 is 2 blocks. How many blocks are 3 quarters?

exercises.prompt: In 5/6, the whole is cut into 5 equal parts.
exercises.hint: Which number says how many parts the whole is cut into?
exercises.explain: No: the bottom number, 6, says the whole is cut into 6 parts; 5 of them are taken.

exercises.prompt: What fraction of the shape is NOT shaded?
exercises.hint: Count all the equal parts, then the white ones.
exercises.explain: 3 of the 8 parts are shaded, so 5 are white: 5/8.

exercises.prompt: Tilly has 24 gems. 3/8 of them are blue. How many blue gems does Tilly have?
exercises.hint: Find 1/8 of 24 first, then take 3 of those.

exercises.prompt: Bram has 30 carrots. He gives 2/5 of them to his buddies. How many carrots does he give?
exercises.hint: Find 1/5 of 30, then take 2 of those.

exercises.prompt: Which is more: 1/3 of 12 or 1/4 of 20?
exercises.explain: 1/3 of 12 is 4 and 1/4 of 20 is 5, so 1/4 of 20 is more.

exercises.prompt: Put these in order, smallest first.
exercises.hint: Work out each one: divide by the bottom number.

exercises.prompt: This wall has room for 12 blocks. Fill 5/6 of it.
exercises.hint: 1/6 of 12 is 2 blocks. How many blocks are 5 sixths?
